    Every representation of the linear quiver is a direct sum of intervals #

    The structure theorem for representations of 1 → 2 → ⋯ → n (the classical fact stated after Definition 5.1 that the interval representations are the indecomposables). The proof is elementary: for a nonzero representation X, let i₀ be the first vertex with X(i₀) ≠ 0, pick a nonzero vector v there and let d be the last vertex to which v survives. The span of the images of v is a copy of M_{i₀,d}, and a linear functional on X(d) with value 1 on the image of v gives a retraction X ⟶ M_{i₀,d} (natural because X vanishes before i₀). Hence M_{i₀,d} splits off, and induction on the total dimension finishes the proof (intervalSum).

    The predicate IntervalSum X records such a decomposition into iterated binary direct sums of intervals.
